title: AMD ROCm — mount and forward
why: Run a Go layer on an AMD GPU with an explicit lifetime via the independent welvet.rocm library.
what: Mount an identity Dense layer, inspect the ROCm version and device identity, and forward a Float32 tensor.
body_extra:
Session ownership

Create a session with nativerocm.Mount, call Forward repeatedly and close it when finished. Mount accepts supported layers, Stack, Parallel and Grid layouts. The library is independent of welvet.cpp, welvet.metal and welvet.cuda.

Requirements and backend boundaries

Go Welvet v1.5.0 adds the independent welvet.rocm 0.79 library (mounted model ABI 1) at github.com/openfluke/welvet.rocm. Install from its checkout:

cd ../welvet.rocm
./scripts/linux_install_go.sh
# Windows amd64 (MSVC + ROCm / HIP):
./scripts/windows_install_go.ps1

Execution requires Linux x86_64 or Windows amd64, Go with cgo, and an AMD driver/runtime with HIP (libamdhip64). Set WELVET_ROCM_LIBRARY to override library discovery. Ordinary Go CPU use does not require an AMD GPU. Unsupported hosts print SKIP; missing libraries or no GPU on a supported host also soft-SKIP in these book examples.

Honest coverage: library build/load is validated; GPU compute remains untested until a ROCm-capable HSA device is available (Polaris/Picasso-class hosts do not qualify).

Go schedules work and manages memory; numerical ROCm forward, backward and weight updates execute device kernels when HSA is present. Activations are Float32; FormatNone parameter storage follows the ROCm dtype matrix. Small examples demonstrate APIs; GPU launch costs can outweigh useful work at small shapes.

cpu-tiled / go_cpu means Go CPU; native_cpu means welvet.cpp; rocm means the independent AMD GPU library. Examples 96–100 can use go run -tags welvet_rocm . to exclude C++ linkage. Chapter 101 requires the normal cgo build for both native engines. JSON routing (§100–§101) is Linux amd64 today; explicit Mount works on Windows amd64 as well.

title: AMD ROCm — Mamba parameter dtypes
why: Exercise native storage formats without changing the activation interface.
what: Run a seeded Mamba forward pass across all 34 native parameter dtypes, or select one with -dtype.
body_extra:
Storage versus arithmetic

-dtype all sweeps native parameter representations. The ROCm execution interface uses Float32 activations. Quantized FormatNone dtype storage and packed quantization formats are different coverage claims.

go run . -dtype all
go run . -dtype float16

Requirements and library installation (Linux + Windows): chapter 96. GPU compute untested until a ROCm-capable HSA device is available.

title: AMD ROCm — training modes
why: Keep repeated training updates in the mounted ROCm session.
what: Train two Dense layers using one of the 29 numbered modes, with persistent Step Line state and real Grid layouts for Mesh modes.
body_extra:
Training families

-mode all exercises all 29 modes. Step modes retain their Line session across calls. Mesh modes use a three-cell Grid with disabled ingress and two active layers, advancing four ticks per call. Bundled welvet.rocm 0.79 covers train modes through StepTweenSplitSparse. These small demonstrations validate usage; they are not performance measurements.

go run . -mode NormalBP -steps 8
go run . -mode all -steps 8

Explicit mounted sessions keep updated weights native until SyncToGo(). Close discards any updates not returned to Go. See chapter 99 before saving.

Requirements: chapter 96.

title: AMD ROCm — weight return and ENTITY save
why: Return trained weights to Go before executing or saving the Go model.
what: Train natively, explicitly SyncToGo, save an ENTITY, reload it and compare the native parameter snapshots.
body_extra:
Weight handoff

session, err := nativerocm.Mount(layer)
// Check err; defer session.Close().
// Repeat session.TrainMSE(...) as needed.
err = session.SyncToGo()
// Check err, then save through Go ENTITY IO.

Mount copies model state into a native session. The original Go parameters stay unchanged while that explicit session trains. SyncToGo() returns parameter bytes, scales and Float64 biases for Go saving. This saves model parameters, not a portable checkpoint of live Line, proxy, KV or rule state.

Use -out /path/model.entity to choose the output location. The default uses a temporary directory and prints it.

Requirements: chapter 96.

title: AMD ROCm — JSON backend placement
why: Choose which layers run on AMD GPU while retaining ordinary Go training entry points.
what: Enable the ROCm router and apply JSON placement to a Stack: layer 0 on Go CPU, layers 1–2 on ROCm.
body_extra:
Explicit placement

The example embeds placement.json; use -config to load another file. nativerocm.EnableRouting() installs the router for its owner lifetime (Linux amd64). placement.Stack applies immediate-child numeric layer keys.

Routed execution maintains native sessions and returns updated parameters to Go automatically. Changing source weights remounts a session and resets transient native state. Automatic hardware/performance planning remains separate from explicit placement.

Windows amd64 supports explicit Mount (chapters 96–99); automatic JSON routing is Linux-only in this release.

Requirements: chapter 96.

title: AMD ROCm — mixed Go/C++/ROCm
why: Split a single model between the independent native engines and Go.
what: Run a 13-layer Dense Stack: Go layers 0–3, C++ layers 4–8 and ROCm layers 9–12; verify actual native calls during training.
body_extra:
Three engines in one Go model

Go CPU [0–3] → welvet.cpp [4–8] → welvet.rocm [9–12] → Go result

The embedded placement.json uses go_cpu, native_cpu and rocm. Install both native libraries and use the normal cgo build (do not pass -tags welvet_rocm). The example reports successful C++ C ABI calls and ROCm routing counters after five NormalBP updates.

Activations and parameters cross backend boundaries. Live backend-specific Line, proxy, KV or rule state is not migrated between engines.

Requirements: Linux amd64 + chapter 96.

title: AMD ROCm — results and suite pointers
why: Find the AMD sibling repo and live ROCm parity/timing matrices after the small usage chapters.
what: Print Go v1.5.0 / welvet.rocm 0.79 pins and commands for w2a go_v_rocm and rocm_smoke. No GPU required.
body_extra:
Where live results live

This chapter is host-only. It does not claim timings from loading the page. Sibling AMD engine: github.com/openfluke/welvet.rocm. Run the matrices on a machine with a ROCm-capable AMD GPU:

cd ../../w2a && go test ./tests/go_v_rocm -count=1 -timeout 180m
cd ../../welvet.rocm/examples/rocm_smoke && go run .
cd welvet/examples && ./run_amd.sh

Engine pin: welvet.rocm 0.79, model ABI 1, Go binding nativerocm (Welvet v1.5.0). Platforms: Linux x86_64 + Windows amd64 for Mount; Linux amd64 for EnableRouting. GPU compute untested until a ROCm-capable HSA device is available.

Requirements overview: chapter 96.
